# GEO report: harbor-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 69/100, Needs work

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 17.33 ÷ 25 × 100 = 69. High = (17.33 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 69.

Everything was decided from code, so the range is a single number. Three things cost points: two AI search crawlers are blocked, the structured data is broken, and every page shares one canonical address. The sampled routes were `/`, `/moorings` and `/contact`, which is all of them. There is no `geo.config.json`, so I assumed you want AI search tools to find the site. The cap of 40 does not apply, because the blocker needs a declared policy to be broken and none is declared.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Let the AI search crawlers in (or declare that you chose not to)
- **Why it matters:** `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search) and `PerplexityBot` are shut out of the whole site, so those tools can't read it to quote it.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` and `User-agent: PerplexityBot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 81/100. If the block is deliberate, say so in `geo.config.json` under `policy.aiSearchCrawlers` and this check changes accordingly.

### 2. Fix the two broken structured data blocks
- **Why it matters:** Structured data (JSON-LD) is a machine-readable label for page facts. Both of yours are malformed, so machines will likely ignore them.
- **Where:** `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`
- **What the code says:** `" ": {` where the key should be `acceptedAnswer`, and `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }` with a trailing comma that makes the JSON invalid.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 77/100

### 3. Give each page its own canonical address
- **Why it matters:** A canonical tells search engines which URL is the main one for a page. Yours says every page is the home page.
- **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`
- **What the code says:** `<link rel="canonical" href="https://harbor.example/" />`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 75/100. Build the URL from `Astro.url.pathname` and a `site` setting.

| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and has required fields | Problem | `faq.json:8`, `moorings.astro:9` (0 of 2) |
| GEO-011 | Valid sitemap is discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt:10` |

## Other problems found

- **Page-wide snippet block on every indexable page:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`: `content={robots ?? "max-snippet:0"}`. This stops AI search tools quoting any text from `/` and `/moorings`. Default to `"index, follow"` or remove the default.
- **A noindex page is listed in the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:5`: `<loc>https://harbor.example/contact</loc>`, while `src/pages/contact.astro:4` sets `robots="noindex"`. Remove it from the sitemap.
- **`/contact` canonicalises to the home page:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`. This is part of the canonical problem above.

## Worth considering

- **Show the FAQ answers on the page:** `src/pages/index.astro:8`: `<script type="application/ld+json" set:html={JSON.stringify(faq)}>`. The answers ("Yes, from May to September.") exist only in the script. Render them as visible text from `faq.json` too.
- **Add `LocalBusiness` or `Organization` structured data:** `src/pages/contact.astro:6`: `Call the harbour office on 01326 000000.` Label the name, phone and Falmouth location. A `Product` or `Offer` could do the same for `Prices start at £40 a night.` (`moorings.astro:7`).
- **Back up the pricing claim:** `src/pages/moorings.astro:7`: `Prices start at £40 a night.` The page promises "Mooring sizes and seasonal prices" in its description but has only this one line. Add a table of sizes and seasonal rates.
- **Link between related pages:** `src/pages/index.astro:7` mentions moorings and a water taxi, but the body has no link to `/moorings` or `/contact`. Add in-text links.
- **Set the site URL in Astro config:** there is no `astro.config.*`, so no `site` value exists. Add `site: "https://harbor.example"`, which also lets you use `@astrojs/sitemap` instead of the hand-kept `public/sitemap.xml`.
- **Add `<lastmod>` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-5` has none.
- **Add head basics and page structure:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:5-10` sets no `charset`, `viewport` or social tags (`og:title`, `og:description`). Wrap the `<slot />` in `<main>`.
- **Make the titles say where and who:** `src/pages/contact.astro:4`: `title="Contact the harbour office"` doesn't name the harbour or town. Add "Falmouth" or the harbour's name.
- **Fix a mixed spelling:** the title `Harbor moorings in Cornwall` (`index.astro:5`) uses "Harbor" while the page text uses "harbour". Pick one so the name is consistent.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which compares real crawler requests with their published addresses.
- **Server responses:** real status codes, redirects and `X-Robots-Tag` headers set at the host. A live scan with your URL would show them.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json`.
- `harbor.example` is a placeholder, so I treated it as the intended origin.
- The noindex on `/contact` is deliberate.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
